text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 2.8% today, rebounding after a volatile week that saw the stock drop 7% from late October highs. The bounce comes as oil refiners face a mixed picture: crude prices remain elevated (US oil at $103/barrel, world oil at $123/barrel), refineries are running near full capacity at 92.8%, and gasoline inventories remain relatively tight at 209 million barrels—conditions that typically support refiner margins and profitability. Marathon's own leadership change and company update announced this week may also be stabilizing the stock after recent uncertainty.

The broader context is that Big Oil earnings are about to be reported, and refining profits have surged despite political pressure—Trump has criticized high energy prices but also called out Big Oil profits, while potential U.S.-Iran negotiations could eventually add more crude supply to the market. For a refiner like Marathon, today's modest gain reflects the tension between strong current margins (driven by tight supplies and high oil prices) and investor caution about what guidance executives will offer given the uncertain geopolitical and political environment ahead.
